correctness.rationale: The decagonal unit sphere is exhausted by edge interiors and vertices. The dihedral isometries reduce these to one reference edge and one reference vertex. At an edge interior, the unique norming functional forces y onto the anti-diagonal and hence y=±(phi,-phi). At the reference vertex, the convex hull of the two active norming functionals gives exactly one opposite edge of admissible y after sign reduction. Exact substitution yields chord pairs (2r+r^2 q, phi-r^2 q) in both branches, so their sum is constant. The balanced parameter q=1/2 gives equal chords and simultaneously proves sharpness for J_perp and g_perp.
risks: The polyhedral norming-functional criterion must be applied to the active signed facets; the proof explicitly handles the edge and vertex subdifferentials.
The finite checker is supplementary; the continuum result rests on the analytic two-case classification.

originality.rationale: The defining 2022 full text was inspected at the definitions, general inequalities, and the complete examples section. It computes two hexagons, the regular octagon, and a mixed Euclidean--taxicab plane, but not the affine-regular decagon. Targeted public-index searches covered the exact parameter names, decagon aliases, the exact candidate value, the chord-sum formulation, and related Birkhoff objectives. No covering record was located. The closest decagonal public record with the same numerical value is a Banach--Mazur distance and has no implication to the Birkhoff chord sum. The current and immediate-prior own ledgers were checked for decagonal Birkhoff and James statements; related rows optimize different objectives or omit the orthogonality restriction.
residual_risks: Bibliographic and semantic-index searches cannot establish absolute novelty.
An equivalent calculation may exist under a linearly equivalent decagon normalization without the J_perp/g_perp notation.
The coincidence with the published-index Banach--Mazur value may reflect an unlocated structural relation, although the located record itself does not imply the present claim.
risks: No independent human literature audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The finding is structural rather than a one-number evaluation: every Birkhoff--James unit pair in a canonical non-Hilbert polygon lies on one affine chord-pair profile with constant total length. This simultaneously resolves two independently defined orthogonality-sensitive constants and identifies a common balanced extremizer. The result also provides a sharp benchmark beyond the hexagon and octagon examples in the defining paper and exposes a nontrivial coincidence of the two orthogonal parameters.
risks: The structural identity is specific to the affine-regular decagon; no general regular-polygon law is claimed.
